observation: Round 1 (detection-only Hough relaxation) was proxy-neutral: 0.5518 -> 0.5453, correspondence_f1@15 0.225 -> 0.213, sam_fill_rate 0.749 -> 0.750, ring_count_error 0, depth_nan_ratio unchanged at 0.223, residual 2.4 cm. Stages 1-3 remain healthy (orient_axis_corr 0.94, invariant OK, retention 0.76, NaN family-normal). The round-1 detected_lines/initial_prompt_points show 10 Hough verticals for 10 rings (kept), oblique yield up from ~5 to ~10 segments and real prompts up from 4 to 5 (1 positive, 3 midpoint, 1 negative; 5 still 'assume' alternating y~1120/1550), but one new oblique line (x 1900-2200, y~750) crosses a ring vertical and is spurious. The lines that DO sit on real intra-ring seams are overwhelmingly the near-horizontal fallback (blue) traces: ~13 of them land exactly on the dotted seam pixels visible in the binarised outlier map, while the 4700x3600 map has ~70 seam segments in total. The SC overlay is therefore line-yield-limited: with only ~15 joint lines against ~70 label boundaries, boundary precision is capped near 0.2 even when every line is explained, so correspondence_f1@15 cannot rise above ~0.3 regardless of prompt quality. Seams appear as sparse dotted traces (gaps ~10-40 px) with faint intensity, dominated by bolt-hole chevrons that are ~100 px apart.
rule: Ontology d7 (m_line_yield low AND horizontal fallback triggered) -> stage_4_detection.f_missing_lines; upstream d6 f_joint_oversmoothed is present (seams faint/dotted in the outlier map) but its remediation r_lower_depth_threshold is outside the bounded space, so the bounded stand-in is r_relax_hough on the path that actually traces seams (horizontal): lower threshold and raise maxLineGap so dotted seam traces join into lines, and lower the binarisation threshold so faint seam pixels survive dilation. maxLineGap_horizontal is capped at 30 px < chevron spacing (~100 px), which guards against f_spurious_lines from bolt rows. Experiences s5 / s8: in the complex family Hough oblique sweeps are weakly identifiable, so the vertical count is left pinned (10/10) and the change is concentrated on seam-trace yield and pattern acceptance (pattern_tolerance to bound) rather than on further oblique relaxation, which round 1 showed adds spurious cross-ring lines. Stages 1-3 and SAM geometry stay at anchor/tunnel priors (experiences s4, s7) so any proxy delta is attributable to detection.
failure_mode: stage_4_detection.f_missing_lines (line-yield-limited correspondence: ~15 joint lines vs ~70 seam boundaries), with residual f_pattern_mismatch (5/10 prompt centres still 'assume' fallbacks)
rationale: Coordinated detection overlay that targets the correspondence ceiling directly. binary_threshold 110 -> 100 (lower bound) admits the faintest dotted seam pixels into the binarised outlier map before the 3x3 dilation, which is what the horizontal Hough needs to see a continuous trace. hough_threshold_horizontal 40 -> 30 and maxLineGap_horizontal 10 -> 25 let HoughLinesP bridge the 10-40 px gaps in dotted seam traces at the fixed minLineLength (105 px) so that many more of the ~70 real seams become detected joint lines; the 30 px gap bound is well below the ~100 px chevron spacing, so bolt rows are not joined into false horizontals. Oblique parameters are held at the round-1 values (35 / 70) because further relaxation produced a spurious cross-ring line without raising correspondence. pattern_tolerance 15 -> 20 (bound) so real intersections that are within 20 px of the K/AB spacing (K 245 px, AB 745 px at 5 mm/px) are kept as prompt centres instead of being replaced by alternating 'assume' points. hough_threshold_vertical untouched: 10 verticals == 10 rings. Denoising, enhancing and SAM keys are left at anchor values; SAM geometry (segment_width 1800 mm matches the observed ~362 px ring pitch) is reserved for round 3 only if per-block coherence remains the weak feature after line yield is fixed. Expected GT-free signal: more cyan (explained) joint lines and more green (supported) boundaries in the SC overlay, correspondence_f1@15 up, sam_fill_rate and ring_count_error unchanged.
